Government sector and crowding out
Empirical evidence for/against basic Solow (Mock Q1)
Open economy accounting: V = K + F, GDP vs GNP, CA = S − I
Open economy two-speed dynamics: k jumps to k*, v crawls
Opening theorem: y^n* always rises; wage caveat for strong savers
Stability conditions: sr̄ < n (open) and n+g+δ+ng > 0 (general)
Feldstein-Horioka regression as measure of capital mobility
General Solow setup: Y = K^α(AL)^(1-α), effective labour, per-effective-worker variables
General Solow steady state: k̃*, balanced growth (k, y, c, w grow at g)
Empirical fit: OLS slope 1.52 vs theory 0.5; λ 0.7% vs theory 5%
MRW production function Y = K^α H^φ (AL)^(1-α-φ); per-effective-worker form
MRW transition equations, Solow equations, phase diagram in (k̃, h̃)
MRW steady state k̃*, h̃*, ỹ* and elasticities (~1 wrt s, ~-2 wrt n+g+δ)
MRW golden rule s_K = α, s_H = φ
MRW cross-country regression: R² 0.63 → 0.79, slope estimates 0.59 and 0.93
Policy implications: education subsidies justified by credit/insurance/externalities/distribution imperfections
Solow with land: production Y = K^α (AL)^β X^κ, z = K/Y transition curve and 4 properties
Steady-state growth rate g^y = (βg − κn)/(β+κ); classical vs modern case
Solow with land + oil: depletion drag, E_t = s_E R_t, R_t = (1−s_E)^t R_0
Land+oil g^y formula with three drags (tech share, population, depletion)
How to numerically simulate the transition equations (Mock Q2 part 2)
Why endogenize technological progress; two flavours (externality vs R&D)
Externality model: A_t = K_t^φ; aggregate PF Y = K^(α+φ(1-α)) L^(1-α); CRS at firm vs IRS at aggregate
Factor prices in externality model and capital share = α from Euler
Three regimes by φ: φ<1 semi-endogenous, φ=1 truly endogenous (AK), φ>1 explosive
Semi-endogenous Ch8: transition equation in k̃, steady state k̃*, growth rate g_se = (1+n)^(φ/(1-φ)) - 1
AK model: Y = AK with A = L^(1-α); truly endogenous growth rate g_e = sA - δ; no convergence; scale effect
R&D production function ΔA = ρ A^φ L_A^λ; standing-on-shoulders φ, stepping-on-toes λ; non-rival ideas
Romer six-equation model: final goods + R&D + capital + labour growth + split + R&D share s_R
Independent dynamics of g_t in Romer: g_{t+1} = (1+n)^λ (1+g_t)^(φ-1) g_t
Semi-endogenous Romer: g_se = (1+n)^(λ/(1-φ)) - 1 ≈ λn/(1-φ); requires n>0
Strictly endogenous Romer: g_e = ρ(s_R L)^λ with φ=1, n=0; scale effect in L
Hemi-endogenous growth (Jones): φ<1, n=0, s_R slowly growing; g_he = λ g_sR / (1-φ); 200-year interpretation
Scale effect critique: bigger countries do not grow faster; 20th-c US population vs growth; Jones researcher-count critique
Empirical investment-rate vs growth-rate correlation; Bernanke-Gürkaynak g_A vs s as endogenous-growth evidence
Population growth vs economic growth: negative correlation contradicts semi-endogenous prediction
Side-by-side: externality (unintentional, perfect competition) vs R&D (deliberate, requires monopoly/patents)
Scale effect and its empirical failure (Jones 1995 critique): researchers rose several-fold but TFP growth stayed flat
Three theories via two knobs: knowledge returns φ (φ<1 vs φ=1) and R&D input (level L_A vs share s_R); semi-endo / Romer-with-scale / truly-endo-without-scale
R&D dilution: population → more sectors → R&D spread thinner → only the share s_R matters (kills the scale effect)
Semi-endogenous growth g^se = (1+n)^(λ/(1−φ)) − 1 ≈ λn/(1−φ); growth chained to n, dies at n=0, policy only temporary
Truly-endogenous growth without scale effect g^e = ρ s_R^λ (φ=1, share s_R); policy permanent; no population/scale dependence
Complete model and per-effective-worker reduction ỹ = k̃^α(1−s_R)^(1−α); k̃ transition with (1+n)(1+g^e) dilution
Steady state k̃* = (s/(n+g^e+δ+ng^e))^(1/(1−α))(1−s_R), ỹ*; per-capita output grows at the technology rate g
Cozzi (2017) hybrid: A-equation as weighted sum of the two mechanisms (weight α_sem ≠ capital share α); hybrid growth rate g_t
Three-case theorem (n=0, n<0, n>0): which mechanism's term survives the A^(φ−1) limit; NOT the naive weighted average (winner-take-all)
Threshold n̄ = [(1−α_sem)ρs_R^λ + 1]^((1−φ)/λ) − 1; n>n̄ → g^se (semi), n<n̄ → (1−α_sem)g^e (endo); demography is the referee
Policy: semi=temporary vs truly=permanent; n̄ rises with s_R so policy can flip the regime ('policy makes policy effective'); Lisbon 1%→3% example; demographic-history arc
Numerical simulation sketch (Mock Q3 'simulate' half): initial A_0 = (ρ(s_R L_0)^λ/g^se)^(1/(1−φ)) on the BGP; g_y response to a drop in n (overshoot ~6 periods then converge lower)
Two-economy calibration (Exercise 5.2): n=0.04 → semi-endogenous g^h=0.054; n=0.02 → fully endogenous g^h=0.046; n̄≈3.4%
Mock Q3 target: derive AND discuss the policy implications of the Cozzi (2017) hybrid model (M5 is mock-exam-load-bearing)

missed_questions.topic_tag: MRW transition and phase diagram — k̃, h̃ are CONSTANT at steady state (only level variables grow at g)
MRW steady-state elasticities — adding H resolves the cross-country savings-rate puzzle (basic Solow predicts ~0.5, MRW ~1, observed ~1.5)
MRW Golden Rule — consumption share = 1−α−φ ≈ labour share (structural symmetry with basic Solow)
Empirical fit — 'adding H = adding a factor' is loose; the sharp mechanism is raising broad-capital elasticity α → α+φ, which moves slope AND convergence speed via the SAME structural shift
Education subsidies — H entering the production function does NOT by itself justify subsidies; positive vs normative distinction (Cozzi p21)
MRW parameter inversion from convergence speed — arithmetic-direction error: solving λ=(1−α−φ)(n+g+δ) for α+φ gives 0.75, not 0.25 (1−x = 0.25 → x = 0.75)
Land model: modern case ($n=0$) gives $g^y = \beta g/(\beta+\kappa) < g$, NOT $g^y = g$ — the diminishing-returns drag never vanishes when $\kappa > 0$

missed_questions.topic_tag: Meaning of φ in the externality model — φ is the elasticity of the knowledge externality A_t = K_t^φ w.r.t. aggregate capital (spillover strength), distinct from the private capital exponent α

AK model properties (MTF) — two cells wrong (C said F, should be T; D said T, should be F); revisit which AK features hold: no transitional dynamics, constant growth g_e = sA−δ, no convergence, scale effect

Factor income shares in the externality model — under perfect competition factors earn PRIVATE marginal products, so capital's income share = α (not the social α+φ(1−α)) despite aggregate increasing returns
Recovering φ from an observed g_se — inverting g_se = (1+n)^(φ/(1−φ)) − 1 for φ; arithmetic-inversion step (same slip class as M3 Q13)
